deliveredReplay.title: VoltGrid: the case, and the questions
deliveredReplay.summary: VoltGrid is a seed climate company. The fictional source pack reports $840,000 annual revenue, including $620,000 ARR. Climate matches your interests. This is a repeatable source-pack replay; founder figures are unaudited, and preference alignment is not a return forecast.

strengths.text: $620,000 ARR is reported separately from total annual revenue of $840,000.
The company reports 68% year-over-year revenue growth. Growth from an early base does not establish durability.
23 paying customers provide an initial traction signal; retention and contract terms still need verification.

risks.text: 14 months of reported cash runway creates a future financing dependency.

The three largest operators contribute 46% of revenue. Utility interconnection and market-participation approvals can delay deployments. There is no active secondary market, no scheduled exit, and no guarantee that the round will close. Investors may lose their entire investment.

diligenceQuestions: Can the founder reconcile the reported financials to bank records and signed customer contracts?
What are retention, customer concentration, and gross margin after all delivery costs?
What milestones does this round fund, and what happens if the next round cannot be raised?
What rights, dilution, transfer restrictions, and eligibility requirements apply to the actual security?
guardrails: Fictional companies and illustrative financials. No live securities are offered.
Preference match is not a return forecast, suitability determination, or investment advice.
Private investments are illiquid; investors may lose their entire investment.
Simulation only: no money moves and no transaction is executed.
